questions.problem: Let $a=⟨3,-4,5⟩$ and $b=⟨2,-6,1⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 2+(-4)\cdot (-6)+5\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{35}{41}⟨2,-6,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{70}{41},-\frac{210}{41},\frac{35}{41}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=⟨2,-4,0⟩$ and $b=⟨9,7,7⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $b$ onto $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{a\cdot b}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 9+(-4)\cdot 7+0\cdot 7}{{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}a \\  & =-\frac{10}{20}⟨2,-4,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}⟨2,-4,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,2,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =-2\cdot x+1\cdot 3+2\cdot 1 \\  & =-2x+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ -2x+5 & =0 \\ 2x & =5 \\ x & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
